## - LTE : Lifting The Exponent -

We conclude this course with an extremely useful theorem in arithmetic. For an integer $n$ and a prime number $p$, we denote by $v_{p}(n)$ the exponent of the highest power of $p$ dividing $n$.

Theorem 12. Let $p$ be an odd prime number. Let $a, b$ be integers (not necessarily positive) and $n \geq 1$ an integer. Suppose that $p$ divides $a-b$ but $p$ does not divide $a$ or $b$. Then:

$$
v_{p}\left(a^{n}-b^{n}\right)=v_{p}(a-b)+v_{p}(n)
$$

This theorem should be known. We refer to the following text:

http ://www.artofproblemsolving.com/Resources/Papers/LTE.pdf

for a proof, extensions to the case $p=2$, and numerous examples of application. We strongly encourage the reader to read this text carefully.
